language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hello, my name is Linda! Meet my friend, Tim! Today, we'll explore this beautiful island. I've brought this Solar System boardgame along; we'll play this too!
Great idea, Linda! This board game looks magnificent. It seems to be representing our solar system, which is full of planets, moons, asteroids, comets, minor planets, and many other exciting objects.
Yeah, we learned about this in school too. Sometimes I wonder how our Solar System was formed…

Linda, scientists believe that the solar system evolved about 4.5 billion years ago from a giant cloud of dust and gas. At the center of this cloud, a small star began to form and eventually ignited forming the Sun. Further away from the center, there were smaller clumps of dust and gas that became the planets, minor planets, moons, comets, and asteroids.
Wow, that's interesting! Tim, how about revising the solar system concepts while exploring this board game?
That's a great idea, Linda! It will be great fun. Let's get started.

In our solar system eight planets circle around the Sun. The Sun in the center while the eight planets travel around it in circular paths called orbits.
That's right, Linda! The inner solar system contains Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. These four planets are closest to the Sun. The outer solar system contains Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Thanks, Tim! Can you help me solve this exercise? All you need to do is select the correct answers and then click the Submit button.

exercises.title: Identify the moons of the planets

dialog.text: Tim, look at the sky! The sun has already started setting. This beach looks so beautiful at dusk... look at the moon... it's gleaming!
Did you know that a moon is a satellite that circles a larger planet? Do you know how many moons are present in our solar system?
You mean there are several other moons in our solar system?
Yes Linda, just like our Earth has a moon, other planets have moons as well!
Thanks, Tim! Can you help me solve this exercise so we can learn more about the moons of our Solar System? All you need to do is select the correct answer.
